Each offer has a defined result and a contract type. Two are fixed price, one is a monthly retainer, and one is time-based. If you are not sure which one fits, the [table below](#which-one) maps common situations to an offer.

## The offers

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}
#### 1 · Agent Reliability Audit
*Fixed price · about 2 weeks*

**For:** teams with an agent or LLM feature in pilot or production who cannot say how often it is right.

**What I do:** build an evaluation set from your real questions and logs, score the current system on the results it returns, and read the traces to classify why it fails.

**You get:** the eval suite in your repository, a baseline accuracy figure with its uncertainty, a failure breakdown, and a ranked list of fixes.
:::

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}
#### 2 · Agent Build Sprint
*Fixed price · 4 to 6 weeks*

**For:** teams that know which agent they want — an analytics agent, Text-to-SQL over the warehouse, a coding-agent workflow for a migration — and need it built and proven.

**What I do:** agree the acceptance test in week one (an eval set and a pass mark), then build to it: grounding, guardrails, tool contracts, evaluation.

**You get:** a working agent in your environment, its results against the agreed pass mark, and a handoff plan for production.
:::

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}
#### 3 · Reliability Retainer
*Monthly fee · a fixed number of days per month*

**For:** teams with agents already in use, where models, prompts, and data keep changing.

**What I do:** re-run the eval suite when something changes, review agent changes before they ship, extend the suite as new failures show up, and answer questions as they come.

**You get:** a monthly regression report, reviewed changes, and a senior engineer who already knows your system.
:::

::: {.g-col-md-6 .g-col-12}
#### 4 · Embedded AI Engineering
*Hourly or daily rate · typically three months or more*

**For:** larger builds, or teams that need a senior engineer or an interim lead inside the team.

**What I do:** join your team and deliver alongside it: agents, data-platform work, migrations with coding agents. When needed I lead the team as well, most recently a 4–7 person data science and analytics team.

**You get:** senior capacity under your own planning, contracted directly or through your consultant broker.
:::

:::

## Which one? {#which-one}

| Your situation | Start with |
|---|---|
| You have an agent or LLM feature and do not know how reliable it is | Agent Reliability Audit |
| You know what you want built and need it proven before you commit further | Agent Build Sprint |
| Your agents are in use, and every model or prompt change is a risk | Reliability Retainer |
| You need a senior engineer or lead in the team for months | Embedded AI Engineering |

The audit is the usual starting point. Its eval suite becomes the acceptance test for a sprint and the regression suite for a retainer.

## How it starts

1. **Intro call** — you describe the system and the problem.
2. **Written scope** — deliverables, the price or rate, and what I need from you (data access, a contact person). For the fixed-price offers the acceptance criteria are part of the scope.
3. **Start** — weekly check-ins, and a written handoff at the end.

## Practicalities

- **Legal entity:** InertialRange Labs AB (Swedish Aktiebolag) — invoicing in SEK or EUR.
- **Location & mode:** based in Linköping, Sweden — remote-first across the Nordics and EU, with onsite for kickoffs and key milestones.
- **Fit:** strongest where there is real data, a real production target, and a stakeholder who wants ownership and evidence — not a strategy deck or a research paper.
- **Confidentiality:** comfortable working under NDA and within existing security/compliance constraints.
